title: GPU hangroot ("shadowrun") incident notes and runbook sketch
body:
Summary:

This is a working incident review and runbook sketch for a recurring class of GPU node hangs we've been seeing across a subset of our fleet over the last 6 weeks. We nicknamed the failure mode 'shadowrun' because the nodes become unresponsive (user workload processes stay alive) while the GPU device stops making forward progress and the kernel logs show a repeating pattern of soft ECC bursts, nvlink negotiation stalls, and an eventual nvidia module reset attempt that sometimes triggers a kernel hang/root panic.

Incident id: SRE-2027-09-SHADOWRUN-01
First observed: 2027-08-31 03:22 UTC (small spike)
Current cluster impact: intermittent node-level degradation, slower scheduling, occasional job restarts for long-running workloads on affected nodes.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- Trigger: micro-burst of correctable ECC errors on one GPU in a DGX-style chassis under low-load idle-to-active transition (usually after a batch schedule change).
- Propagation: ECC bursts are associated with NVLink retrains between the two GPUs in the local NV fabric; retrain/retry loops increase PCIe/NVLink stalls.
- Failure: The nvidia driver attempts a recovery, drains the GPU for reset; in ~10% of cases the driver reset path deadlocks due to a race between the reset thread and the kernel's process context (possible call to driver->resume while GPU IRQs are wedged), which surfaces as a kernel oops/hangroot.
- Observed correlation: nodes with older firmware/retimer firmware and one specific kernel patch level (linux-6.4.x + nvidia 540.x) are disproportionately represented.

Why this is different from prior ECC surge notes:
- The hangroot pattern shows kernel-level stack traces (see excerpt) instead of repeated successful resets or automatic quarantining.
- Recovery frequently requires a cold reboot; warm reset sometimes leaves the device in a half-functional state.

Key evidence (raw):
- dmesg excerpt (sanitized):
  Aug 31 03:22:14 node-12 kernel: [54000.123456] nvidia: GPU 0: ECC correctable error burst (count=23)
  Aug 31 03:22:14 node-12 kernel: [54000.123789] nvlink: lane negotiation timeout on link 1
  Aug 31 03:22:15 node-12 kernel: [54000.223001] nvidia: attempting GPU reset (pid=8742)
  Aug 31 03:22:15 node-12 kernel: [54000.223500] nvidia: reset thread stalled, dumping stack
  Aug 31 03:22:16 node-12 kernel: [54000.223900] Kernel panic - not syncing: hung task: nvidia_reset

- sar/iostat show no host-side CPU or IO saturation at time of event (so not a host-induced spike).
- Telemetry: in-VM GPU metrics show falling PCIe link width intermittently during transition windows.

Reproduction attempts so far (short):
- Synthetic workload replayed (small startup latency bursts) on two spare nodes with older retimer firmware: reproduced ECC bursts + nvlink renegotiation loop but did NOT cause kernel panic — instead driver recovered after ~45s.
- Replayed on newer nodes with linux-6.4.18 + nvidia-540.42: reproduced full hangroot (kernel oops) 2/5 runs.
- Warm reset sequence captured via serial console shows driver reset thread context switching while IRQ handlers are queued.

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Alerting: added new SLO alert SRE-GPU-HANGROOT to detect pattern: repeated correctable ECC > 10 in 60s + nvlink lane timeout events.
- Quarantine: nodes matching ECC+NVLink pattern are auto-drained (kubernetes) and set to cordon state. Manual override available for emergency runs.
- Firmware: coordinate with hardware team to mark chassis with old retimer firmware as low-priority for ML jobs and prefer shard placement for CPU-only or non-critical workloads.

Suggested runbook (draft) - for oncall engineer:
- Symptom detection:
  1) Pager fires for SRE-GPU-HANGROOT or node enters NotReady with GPU errors.
  2) ssh to node via jump host (use bastion with serial privileges if unreachable).
- Initial triage commands (collect these before rebooting):
  - journalctl -k --no-pager --since "1 hour ago" | sed -n '1,300p' > /tmp/kernel-log.txt
  - dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
  - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,REPAIR,LINK > /tmp/gpu-query.txt
  - cat /proc/interrupts | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/interrupts.txt
  - ethtool -S ens6f0 (to check NIC link errors)
  - lspci -vv -s $(lspci | grep -i nvidia | awk '{print $1}') > /tmp/lspci.txt
  - iwdev-query and retimer-fw-check: /usr/local/bin/retimer-fw-version || echo unknown > /tmp/retimer-version.txt
  - If node unresponsive for SSH: capture serial console logs (console-logs-YYYYMMDD.txt) and attach.
- Quick containment:
  1) kubectl drain node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
  2) set node annotation gpu:quarantined=true and add to monitoring group for manual firmware upgrade job.
- Attempt soft-recovery (only if business-critical and low risk):
  1) sudo systemctl stop kubelet; sudo rmmod nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia || true
  2) wait 30s, check dmesg for any modprobe messages, modprobe nvidia && modprobe nvidia_modeset
  3) run nvidia-smi --gpu-reset=0 (if supported) and re-check ECC counters.
  Note: if driver reset thread is blocked, unloading modules may hang the kernel — proceed only if you have serial/console access and a watch to reboot if it stalls.
- If soft-recovery fails or kernel shows oops: schedule cold reboot and escalate to hardware team.

Longer-term remediation candidates (backlog):
- Patch/rollback matrix: test linux-6.4.x variants and nvidia-540.x vs 525.x on staging with the synthetic replay harness.
- Retimer firmware push: fleet-wide audit + staged upgrade for retimer firmware; instrument per-chassis telemetry of link retrain counters.
- Driver change: engage with NVIDIA support (NVTS ticket) with collected serial logs and oops stacks; request guidance on reset deadlock fix or backported driver patch.
- Kernel lock analysis: reproduce with debug symbols enabled to capture lockdep traces and stack traces of reset thread.
- Eviction heuristics: add preemptive eviction when ECC bursts > threshold to avoid entering reset path under heavy NVLink contention.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does newer driver/kernel combination increase chance of kernel oops for the same ECC patterns? Is a race introduced by the reset path change?
- Are specific host BIOS/PCIe root complex settings (ASP/ART) contributing to link width flapping?
- Do some workloads trigger a corner-case due to simultaneous PCIe active power state changes + NVLink retrain?
- Can we design a non-invasive test that stimulates the edge-case without risking production instability?

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Mateo: build an orchestrated synthetic stress harness that does controlled idle->burst transitions on 3 node types (old-retimer, new-retimer, upgraded-driver). ETA: 2027-09-21
- Priya: open NVTS ticket with attached sanitized serial logs and oops stacks; request triage. ETA: 2027-09-15
- Jon: create a kernel debug staging image with lockdep and repro harness, boot on one spare node. ETA: 2027-09-18
- Aisha (me): update SRE runbook with these steps and fold into Confluence. ETA: 2027-09-16

Notes to self / rough snippets:
- When running synthetic harness, ramp TTL between restarts to find sweet spot (0.5s -> 10s).
- Add an agent to collect nvlink retrain counts from GPU perf counters every 10s for 48 hours post-firmware upgrade.
- Consider a small kprobe on nvidia_reset entry to timestamp entry/exit and detect long holds.

References and context links:
- See related fleet quarantine automation: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/ops/gpu-quarantine.md
- Prior ECC-surges timeline: Confluence ECC-SURGE-2027

Appendix: sample kernel oops stack (sanitized):
  Call Trace:
    nvidia_reset+0x1a4/0x380
    ? do_gpu_reset+0x40/0x40
    ? nvlink_handle_timeout+0x120/0x1a0
    ? __schedule+0x5e0/0x800
    kthread+0x110/0x190

End of working draft. This doc is intentionally rough — add findings, paste full collected logs, and update runbook steps after the first reproducible test is completed.
